title: Robert Fulton, Engineer and Artist: His Life and Works
version: 1913 John Lane edition, Cornell University Library scan.
lineage: The book reproduces original correspondence, maker drawings and the text of the 1808 enrollment. The archive ordinals and contemporary docket are separately identifiable in the Birmingham finding aid.

passages.locator: pp. 177–178, Boulton & Watt account of 17 January and letter of 21 February 1805
passages.note: The account names Robert Fulton and specifies engine materials for a 24-inch cylinder and four-foot stroke. Boulton & Watt’s letter says the goods were forwarded for delivery to his London address.

passages.locator: pp. 230–231, Fulton to Boulton & Watt, 15 September 1810 (MS 3147/3/496, item 15)
passages.note: Fulton identifies the engine made for him in 1804, with a 24-inch cylinder and four-foot stroke, as powering a boat carrying passengers between New York and Albany. He separately orders another engine.
The new enrollment names the North River Steamboat of Clermont, records that the vessel was enlarged, and refers back to enrollment 973 issued in September 1807.

passages.locator: p. 174 and facing plates, cylinder and condenser drawing
passages.note: The reproduced shop drawing is headed R. Fulton and dated 13 September 1804. Dickinson’s caption applies the later Clermont name.
